newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-IAAF THREATEN TO BAN NORWAY AFTER DRUGS SCANDAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IAAF THREATEN TO BAN NORWAY AFTER DRUGS SCANDAL.

text.p: International athletics official said on Monday they would ban Norway from the sport if it failed to report positive drugs tests on time.
The International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) is annoyed that Norway has reported only in the last few days the name of an athlete who tested positive for banned substances on May 14.
IAAF spokesman Giorgio Reineri said on Monday that the governing body had sent a strong letter to the Norwegian federation warning it of the possible suspension.

"The IAAF has sent letters to the Norwegian federation to ask to know the name of the athlete. It has only now just been given to us," he said. "Norway has been warned that if they repeat this they are in danger of being suspended."
A suspension would prevent all Norwegian athletes from competing in all IAAF-run events such as the world championships.

The name of the Norwegian athlete has not been made public but it is not believed to be a major international figure. The athlete has been caught cheating with steroids and is now in danger of being banned for four years.
The IAAF council, meeting a few days before the start of the world championships, decided to take no further action in a controversial case involving athletes from the hosts Greece.
World indoor 60 metres champion Haralambros Papadias was among a group of Greek athletes being investigated by the IAAF after their coach scuffled with a dope tester in Germany in February.

A German tester alleged he was pushed by an angry Greek coach when he was trying to carry out random doping tests in Dortmund. The official said the Greek athletes left the stadium before he was able to test them.
Refusing a test is regarded as being as serious as providing a positive test and the Greek athletes could have been banned.

The Greek federation suspended coach Hristos Tzekos for two years after the incident but no action has been taken against the athletes and Papadias is free to compete at the world championships which open on Friday.

The IAAF agreed with the Greek federation that there were technical difficulties with the case since the tester did not show the necessary identification and appeared at the track alone. Usually a male and female official would appear together for such tests.
"The council accepted these arguments," IAAF general secretary Istvan Gyulai said.
